newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian negotiator heads for new Chechen talks.
newsitem.headline: Russian negotiator heads for new Chechen talks.

text.p: Russian Security Council secretary Ivan Rybkin left Moscow on Thursday for talks with top Chechen separatist officials, Russian news agencies quoted government sources as saying.

Rybkin will meet leading Chechen negotiators Movladi Udugov and Akhmed Zakayev just days after a string of attacks on Russian forces around the region, which has been largely under separatist control since military advances in August.
The Security Council press service declined to comment on the trip.
The officials will meet at the home of the president of Ingushetia, a region neighbouring Chechnya, the sources said.

Rybkin and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin discussed Chechnya on Wednesday, when an unknown group kidnapped two Russian policemen and the bodies of four Russian servicemen were reported found outside the Chechen capital, Grozny.
Chechnya was also on the agenda of a meeting of the new cross-party Consultative Council on Thursday, which Chernomyrdin chaired and Rybkin attended.
On Saturday, 68 people -- most of them border guards -- were killed in a blast at an apartment block in the southern region of Dagestan, neighbouring Chechnya.
A fragile ceasefire agreed in August has yet to lead to a permanent political settlement. Both sides say they hope for a series of accords before Chechen elections in January.
